sources.citation: Quint, Nicolas. 2024. Djifanghor Nyun (Baïnounk). In Lüpke (ed.), Oxford Guide, 291-317 (sister variety gube1234)
sources.note: Nearest-relative context only: 'JFG is a stress language.. stress generally falls on the lexical root.. first syllable of the root, otherwise the heaviest syllable'; demarcative. Not a statement about Gujaher.

sources.citation: Crossroads project site (soascrossroads.org, the Internet Archive 2016-2024): 'The Crossroads languages', 'Publications' pages; Lüpke/Watson/Hantgan talk handouts and drafts (2014-2017)
sources.note: All sociolinguistic; zero linguistic 'stress' tokens. Publications page lists 'Hantgan, Abbie. In prep. Impacts of stress systems among Atlantic languages' for the Oxford Guide, but no such chapter is in the published book (Crossref chapter list) and no such paper exists on Crossref/HAL.

sources.citation: Cobbinah, Alexander Yao. 2017. Suffixed plurals in Baïnounk languages: agreement patterns and diachronic development. JALL 38(2): 145-185. DOI 10.1515/jall-2017-0007
sources.note: Gujaher plural data (from Lüpke); nothing on stress, accent or tone.

sources.citation: Cobbinah, Alexander Yao. 2013. Nominal classification and verbal nouns in Baïnounk Gubëeher. PhD thesis, SOAS (sister language gube1234); Table 4 p. 36 survey of Nyun literature
sources.note: Not Gujaher. Its literature table lists for Gujaher only Bühnen 1988 (ms. wordlist) and de Lespinay 1992 (ms. dictionary) plus Wilson 2007; no stress statement anywhere in the thesis.

sources.citation: Lüpke, Friederike. 2010. Language and identity in flux: in search of Baïnounk. Journal of Language Contact THEMA 3: 155-174 (whole issue PDF, 287 pp.)
sources.note: Sociolinguistic survey of Baïnounk varieties; nothing on stress/accent/tone (all 14 'stress' tokens in the issue are non-linguistic). Identity: Wilson's 'Banhum/Gujaaxǝr' = the southern Gu-jaaxǝt variety (citing Sapir 1971:61); BOREPAB labels Gunyaamolo/Gubaher/Gujaher (Samik area). Same issue: Childs' Table 3 'Accent and tone in Atlantic' (23 languages, from Childs 1995b) without naming Baïnounk; Cobbinah 2010 on Gubaher has no phonology.

sources.citation: Lüpke, Friederike. 2024. Baïnounk Gujaher. In F. Lüpke (ed.), The Oxford Guide to the Atlantic Languages of West Africa, 318-345. Oxford: OUP.
